title: This Is Why I Still Don't Trust Codex By Itself
author: bingewavecinema

comments.author: BertJohn
comments.body: Trying to vibecode with just prompts will always result in failure. You must have an explicit .md sheet ready for it to reference constraints like this.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: I don’t think .md sheets are enough. You usually need some kind of system capable of checking constraints. Something like a test suite can work, sometimes (being vague because there are a lot of options).

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body:
The only thing you need are more .md sheets. 

  
You can pre-plan entire construction phases of a code base and adhere and update the phase output to a new .md sheet so you can clear context and pickup right where it needs to know what to do next.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: More instructions, to fix the problem that your AI doesn’t always follow instructions! Just send in more instructions!

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body: Sounds like your giving impossible or too vague of an instruction then because only through implementing multi-phase .md instruction sheets with comprehensive instruction on things to avoid or do has resulted in it doing as instructed. If you are instructing it and it is producing something you did not expect, your instructions sucked and needs to be more concise.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: No, that’s false. This is a known problem with LLMs.

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body:
No... LLM's are doing exactly as instructed. If you tell an LLM to go write hello world in unity and not to use the print feature, Its going to ask itself how does the user want it written, and in what medium, well it didnt say any other constraints so i can use cubes at this scale to write this out and position the camera here to see the words hello world. It will approximate the positions and scales of the words because it can't "imagine" the space but approximate mathematically the positions and scales necessary to build the shapes necessary. 

  
Did it do what you wanted? Technically yes. Did it do it how it should have been done? No. Could the user have been more precise that you wanted something else? Absolutely. 

  
When constructing .md sheets, you need to proof read the entire sheet, even after passing it through an LLM, How is the AI going to try to construct this with the limitations provided. 

  
Low reasoning efforts also result in lower contextual input, So if this is what your basing LLM's capabilities on, You need to upgrade to pro atleast and come join sol on medium/high where its multi-agent processing really kicks in.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
LLMs do not “do exactly as instructed”; they generate probable continuations conditioned on inputs, which can be misunderstood, inconsistently followed, or outweighed by patterns in training data. That’s why their behavior needs to be tested rather than assumed.

If you want to effectively use LLMs you give them a feedback loop they can use to check whether the output is correct.

LLMs will do fine if you give them something super easy, like “Write hello world without print”, but that’s kind of trivial and not very interesting.

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body:
You literally argued against yourself in your post. Congratulations, you played yourself. 

  
Yes, LLM's convert the inputs and follow the most probable line of data to get to what the user desires as the most probable outcome based off training data. This is LLM 101. 

  
There behaviour is extensively tested all the time, theres 4 major firms out there right now that test all LLM's for jailbreak techniques and are responsible for Sol & Fable 5 being locked down. 

  
LLM's do fine if you give them clear and concise instructions. It has no matter or suitability to what its actually making, whether it be hello world or converting GPU RGBA to simulate civilization data framework structure or memory management. LLM's aren't like humans where writing print hello world is conceptually easy for us to understand, Its quite the opposite as i posted in my post above. The LLM has no imagination, it can approximate mathematically the dimensions of hello world based on what it knows about the alphabet and spacing on a grid. That is complex for the LLM. But writing out a management application to manage a database for renters for a landlord or writing out a complex orientation graph to connect an auto-resolving river system in a game is all regular childs play for an LLM. 

  
Lastly, LLM's are not like you or i, They can't be babysat and audited the entire time and expected to produce a perfect result in one pass. Your LLM will consistently auto-fill contextual items you are not factoring in for or yet, first, And build the item first, and then will pass through again later addressing items like OP's post. But OP, Being impatient and not understanding how LLM's work, steered the conversation to address a concern they had right away, instead of letting it cook the product first and then fixing it afterwards. 

  
This is why i say not everyone should be allowed to use AI because they don't know enough about how it works and how to maximize the usage of their tokens.
